task.description: Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0401. Read docs/issues/ISS-0401.yaml in full first. Symptom: test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:392-394's `assert function_exported?(Repository, :upsert_content, 6)` fails (returns false) even though lib/letflow/repository.ex:251 defines a genuinely public `upsert_content/6` with a matching @spec, confirmed present in the compiled module via `Letflow.Repository.__info__(:functions)` (which DOES show it). This is a real, reproducible discrepancy between `function_exported?/3` and `__info__(:functions)` for the same module/function/arity -- not a typo or a missing function. Reproduce it directly yourself first (do not trust the prior report's prose alone, per No Speculation): run `mix test test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:392` standalone and confirm the failure, then use `mix run -e` or an IEx-equivalent one-liner to directly compare `function_exported?(Letflow.Repository, :upsert_content, 6)` against `Letflow.Repository.__info__(:functions) |> Enum.filter(fn {n,_} -> n == :upsert_content end)` in the same BEAM session, to confirm the exact discrepancy. Root-cause it: the most likely explanation (per the issue's own filing note) is that `function_exported?/3` requires the target module to already be *loaded* into the VM (not merely compiled to a .beam on disk), and returns false for a compiled-but-not-yet-loaded module, while `__info__(:functions)` implicitly triggers a load as a side effect of being called -- but verify this is actually what's happening (e.g. by checking `:code.is_loaded(Letflow.Repository)` before and after the assertion, or by adding a deliberate `Code.ensure_loaded?/1` call ahead of the assertion and confirming that alone fixes it) rather than assuming. Also check whether this is specific to test run order/parallelism (does it fail when this test file is run alone vs. as part of the full suite; does test order within the file matter) since the original filing noted uncertainty about test-ordering interaction. Do NOT implement the fix -- produce a diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER (or determine directly, if the fix is truly a one-line `Code.ensure_loaded?/1` guard with no design decision to make, whether this qualifies for ORCH's own direct-action sizing rule per docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10 -- state your assessment either way in the diagnosis, but the routing decision itself is ORCH's, not yours).
acceptance_criteria: The failure is reproduced directly (real `mix test` run, real output quoted), not inferred from the issue filing's prose alone
The function_exported?/3 vs __info__(:functions) discrepancy is directly demonstrated in the same BEAM session (e.g. via a one-off script or IEx-equivalent), not merely asserted
Whether `:code.is_loaded?/1` (or Code.ensure_loaded?/1) actually explains and fixes the discrepancy is empirically checked, not assumed
Test-order/parallelism sensitivity is checked (standalone run vs. full-file run vs. full-suite run)
Diagnosis states what a fix needs to change, without writing the actual fix

Diagnosis states an explicit assessment of whether this qualifies for ORCH's direct-action sizing rule (single file, no new public function/module/@spec, no migration, no supervision-tree file, no tenant-data path, no test's expected value changes) so ORCH can route correctly

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for 'function_exported'. Two prior related-class entries found, both status: resolved but at least one reopened -- ISS-0340 (Context.scoped_repo_opts/1 1-arity check, first 'resolved' 2026-08-26 by relocating the test out of a tenant-provisioning describe block on the theory that a too_many_connections DB error was marking the unreachable assertion as failed under 16-way parallel load, then REOPENED 2026-08-27 when it recurred under scripts/test_parallel.sh -- the relocation fix did not hold) and ISS-0350 (a different MAJOR issue whose root note independently observed the same class: 'intermittent function_exported? false-negative for execute_with_manifest/2 under the full mix test suite, 1-in-3 runs... reproduces and clears independently' of an unrelated code change). Neither is an exact symptom match (different function/module, and both were framed as full-suite/parallel-load-only flakiness) but both are the same failure class (function_exported? false-negative). ISS-0340's history is a cautionary precedent: its first 'resolved' fix addressed a coincidental DB-connection symptom, not the actual function_exported?/module-loading mechanism, and the underlying issue came back. This run's finding (below) is DIFFERENT from ISS-0340's diagnosis in one load-bearing way: THIS failure is 100% standalone-reproducible with zero parallelism/DB load involved (see below), so it is not a recurrence of ISS-0340's specific connection-pool mechanism, but it is evidence that the module-loading mechanism ISS-0401's own filing note hypothesized is real and has now been directly measured for the first time in this project, where the two prior sightings only inferred it from correlation with parallel load.

STEP 1 (diagnose) -- ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED, MECHANISM DIRECTLY MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED:

1. REPRODUCED: `mix test test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:392` (standalone, single test, no other file, no parallelism) fails deterministically, 100% of 5 consecutive reruns with different random seeds: 'Expected truthy, got false / code: assert function_exported?(Repository, :upsert_content, 6)'. Confirmed after a fresh `mix compile --force` (rules out a stale .beam) and confirmed the .beam file on disk genuinely exports upsert_content/6 via a direct `:beam_lib.chunks/2` read of `_build/test/lib/letflow/ebin/Elixir.Letflow.Repository.beam` (bypasses the VM's loaded-module state entirely) -- so this is not a missing/misnamed function, and not a compiler artifact problem.

2. MECHANISM DIRECTLY MEASURED (not inferred): temporarily instrumented the test (reverted after, `git status --porcelain test/` empty, confirmed) to print `:code.is_loaded(Repository)` immediately before and after the `function_exported?/3` call. Result when run standalone via `:392`: `is_loaded BEFORE: false`, `function_exported?/3 result: false`, `is_loaded AFTER: false` (still false -- function_exported?/3 does NOT trigger a load as a side effect, it just silently returns false for an unloaded module). When the same instrumented assertion runs as part of the FULL file (`mix test test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs`, 18 tests, sequential, async: false), it passes every time (3/3 reruns) -- because 17 earlier tests in the same file already call into `Letflow.Repository` (via `Letflow.Repository.Attachments.upload/2`, `Repo.get!(Artifact, ...)`, etc.), which loads the module as an ordinary side effect of calling its functions, before this test's turn ever comes.

3. CONFIRMED FIX MECHANISM (not implemented as the real fix -- this was a probe, per WF-03 Step 1's 'do not implement the fix' rule): adding a single line, `Code.ensure_loaded?(Repository)`, immediately before the assertion, with NO other change, flips the standalone `:392` run from FAIL to PASS deterministically. This directly confirms Code.ensure_loaded?/1 (not merely __info__/1, which was never actually exercised as 'the thing that loads it' -- see next point) is a sufficient fix.

4. ONE CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE FILING'S OWN HYPOTHESIS: the filing's 'likely cause' prose says '__info__(:functions) implicitly triggers a load as a side effect of being called.' That specific claim was NOT confirmed and is not actually necessary to explain the bug -- what actually loads Repository in every passing scenario observed here is ordinary application code calling one of its functions (Repo.insert/2 via upsert_content/6 itself, or any other Repository.* call), not a bare __info__/1 introspection call. I did not find a code path that calls __info__(:functions) ahead of this test. The bare mechanism is simpler than the filing's note: Elixir/Erlang modules are compiled-and-on-disk but NOT auto-loaded into a given BEAM process's code table until something first calls a function on them (or explicitly loads them) -- function_exported?/3 checks the loaded-module table and returns false, silently, for a genuinely-existing-but-not-yet-loaded module, rather than loading it first. In the ordinary `mix test` (whole-suite or whole-file) case this is invisible because dozens of other tests call Repository functions first. It is only visible in this exact test because it is the ONLY test in its describe block, is a pure introspection test with no Repo/Attachments call of its own, and -- when run via `mix test <file>:<line>` -- ExUnit's `--only location:{file,line}` filter still compiles and loads test *modules* but does not need to load every *application* module referenced only by other (excluded) tests in the same file; when this exact test happens to run first/alone, Repository has never yet been called into.

5. TEST-ORDER / PARALLELISM SENSITIVITY -- explicitly checked, is NOT the deciding factor here (unlike ISS-0340/ISS-0350's framing): failure is 100% reproducible running this ONE test alone, with mix's default max_cases: 32 but only 1 test in the run (so no real concurrency), zero DB/connection load, 5/5 reruns with fresh random seeds. It is a matter of WHICH other tests, if any, ran first and touched Letflow.Repository -- not of timing, load, or parallel scheduling. Running the whole attachments_test.exs file (18 tests, sequential) passes 3/3 reruns because earlier tests load the module first. This means the failure is fully deterministic given 'which tests ran before this one in this process', not flaky/probabilistic -- CI's full-suite run likely passes today only because many other files/tests touching Letflow.Repository run before this one in the same test process; it is one test-selection command away from failing 100% of the time (already reproduced: `mix test test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:392` alone, which is exactly what a developer would naturally run while iterating on just this test, or what test-runner tooling might select when re-running only a previously-failed test).

6. WHAT A FIX NEEDS TO CHANGE (no fix implemented, per WF-03 Step 1 -- routing to CODE-DESIGNER/ELIXIR-DEV, not done here): the test at test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs:391-395 needs to force-load Letflow.Repository before asserting function_exported?/3 against it -- e.g. `Code.ensure_loaded?(Repository)` (confirmed sufficient, see point 3) or equivalently `Code.ensure_loaded!(Repository)` (raises instead of returning false, arguably clearer intent for a test-only assertion) as the first line of the test body, immediately before the assert. This is a 1-line, single-file change to a test file only -- no application code, no @spec, no schema/migration, no new public function, and the test's asserted VALUE does not change (it still asserts the same true/false-shaped fact: upsert_content/6 is exported). No design decision is required beyond picking ensure_loaded?/1 vs ensure_loaded!/1, which is a matter of test-idiom preference, not architecture.

7. SIZING-RULE ASSESSMENT (docs/agents/ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10 -- stated explicitly per this handoff's acceptance criteria; the routing decision itself is ORCH's, not mine): this fix appears to satisfy the plain-language sizing description given in this handoff's task ('single file, no new public function/module/@spec, no migration, no supervision-tree file, no tenant-data path, no test's expected value changes'). Concretely: (a) single file -- only test/letflow/repository/attachments_test.exs changes; (b) no new public API -- lib/letflow/repository.ex is untouched, upsert_content/6 already exists exactly as designed/shipped; (c) no migration or supervision-tree file touched; (d) not a tenant-data path (it is a pure module-introspection assertion, no Repo query, no tenant schema involved in the fix itself, though the surrounding file does use tenant fixtures in OTHER tests); (e) the test's asserted expected VALUE is unchanged -- it still asserts function_exported?(Repository, :upsert_content, 6) is true, only the reliability of observing that true value changes. I have not independently read ORCHESTRATOR.md section 10's actual six-item checklist verbatim in this turn (out of my role's scope per Instruction Precedence -- ORCH owns that document's application), so this is my assessment against the criteria as restated in my own handoff's task.description, not a certified pass against the canonical checklist text itself.
